title: We Were Made for More
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Life teaches us to settle for low expectations. But we were made for more, and in Jesus every longing is not only met but vastly exceeded.
exhortation: We all have a longing, a deep yearning for something we usually can't even put into words. We feel it when we hear a great piece of music, see a breathtaking view, or watch a well-written story play out on screen.

But when the feeling fades and life goes on, we start to settle. We stop expecting greatness. Everything seems disappointing and formulaic, and our expectations sink lower still. We settle into a life of low expectations because it hurts a little less that way. People disappoint us. Music doesn't move us like it used to. We fall asleep halfway through the movie.

But that isn't what we were made for. We weren't made to settle. We were made for more. There is something that won't disappoint: a person who won't let us down, and a story that keeps getting more and more thrilling. In the person of Jesus we have it all. All our hopes, desires, needs and wants are not only met but vastly exceeded. It's time to turn away from the promises of this world that don't deliver and lift our eyes to Jesus, the radiance of God's glory.
prayer: Lord, thank you for being with us through the whole race. You didn't save us and call us only to abandon us. Show us any area where we have given up and surrendered ground to the flesh, the world or the enemy, or where we have accepted a halfhearted, lukewarm existence.

You call all of us, at every stage of life and whatever our physical ability, to press hard in prayer, in love for others, and in the works you have prepared for us. It is a lie that we are no longer useful or can't accomplish anything. You have prepared works for us to do in advance. Let us step into the mission and calling you have for us, fix our eyes on you, Jesus, above all else, and remember how great a salvation we have received, so that we walk and live in it, washed by your blood. Thank you, Jesus.
